# Extreme Networks — ExtremeXOS (EXOS) — Overview

## CLI dialect / platform scope

- **Dialect family**: **ExtremeXOS (EXOS)**, also currently rebranded by Extreme as "Switch Engine" in newer documentation trees (`switchengine_commands_*` URLs are the same command set as `exos_commands_*` — Extreme appears to be renaming the doc property, not changing the CLI). Runs on the Summit/X-series and newer fixed-form and modular (BlackDiamond/SLX-adjacent Extreme-branded) switch lines.
- **Structurally distinct command style — this is the single most important fact for SignalScope's cross-vendor abstraction work.** Every other vendor covered so far (Cisco IOS-XE, Arista EOS, Huawei VRP, Aruba) uses a **context/sub-mode grammar**: enter global config, then enter an interface sub-mode (`interface GigabitEthernet0/1`), and subsequent commands apply implicitly to whatever context you're in. **EXOS does not work this way.** There is no persistent "you are now inside port 1:3" context. Instead, almost every configuration command takes the port(s) or VLAN name as an explicit argument on a single line, e.g.:
  - `configure vlan accounting add ports 1:1, 1:2, 1:3 tagged` — not `interface ...` then `switchport ...`.
  - `enable port 1:3` / `disable port 1:3` — not `interface 1:3` then `no shutdown`/`shutdown`.
  - `configure ports 1:3 description-string "uplink-to-core"` — one line, no sub-mode entry/exit at all.

  There is also no separate "privileged EXEC" vs. "user EXEC" split the way Cisco/Arista have — an EXOS CLI session (once logged in with a sufficiently privileged account) can issue `configure`/`create`/`enable`/`disable` verbs directly. This matters for SignalScope's session-state tracking (per `gui-cli-snmp-unification.md`): where Cisco/Arista/Huawei require tracking "what mode/context is this session currently in" so the GUI knows whether it must first emit `interface X`, **EXOS requires no such context-tracking** — every emitted command is self-contained and could in principle be issued in any order without worrying about a stale sub-mode. This is a genuinely different shape of problem for the unification layer, worth flagging explicitly in the vendor comparison matrix.
- **Ruckus ICX is a separate, distinct dialect that Extreme now also owns** (via the 2022 acquisition of the former CommScope/Ruckus wired portfolio, itself descended from Brocade FastIron, itself descended from Foundry Networks). Ruckus ICX switches run **FastIron**, not EXOS, and its CLI is the classic Cisco-IOS-like context/sub-mode style (`configure terminal` → `interface ethernet 1/1/1` → `no shutdown` — well-known enough that Ruckus/Brocade publish a dedicated [Cisco IOS ↔ ICX command-equivalence deployment guide](https://support.alcadis.nl/Support_files/Ruckus/ICX//Ruckus%20Best%20Practice%20Guide/Brocade%20ICX%20and%20Cisco%20IOS%20Deployment%20Guide.pdf)). Ruckus ICX enterprise SNMP objects still live under the legacy Foundry private-enterprise number **1991** (`FOUNDRY-SN-ROOT-MIB`, `enterprises.1991`), not Extreme's own PEN 1916 — the two product lines have never been merged at the MIB level as of this research. **This document does not cover ICX CLI/MIB syntax in depth** — noting its existence and Cisco-like shape is sufficient for SignalScope's vendor-detection logic (e.g. via `sysObjectID`, which will resolve to a `1.3.6.1.4.1.1991.*` arc for ICX vs. `1.3.6.1.4.1.1916.*` for EXOS) to route an ICX device to the Cisco-family CLI-handling code path rather than the EXOS one. A dedicated ICX deep-dive should be its own future assignment if SignalScope adds first-class ICX support.

## SNMP version support

- **v1**: supported, community-string only.
- **v2c**: supported, community-string only, adds `GETBULK`/64-bit counters. `configure snmp add community` covers both v1 and v2c community strings (EXOS does not appear to separate v1 vs v2c community configuration into distinct commands — the same community entries serve both).
- **v3**: supported, configured under the `configure snmpv3 add ...` command family (`user`, `group`, `access`, `mib-view`, `community` [SNMPv3's own community-to-security-name mapping, distinct from the v1/v2c command above], `target-params`, `notify`, `target-addr`). USM auth is MD5/SHA; privacy is DES/3DES/AES (128/192/256). See `cli-reference.md` and `mib-reference.md` for the concrete command syntax and the distinctive **`mib-view`** access-control mechanism.
- All three versions can be active simultaneously; EXOS also has a documented "SNMPv1/v2c enable/disable" and separate "SNMPv3 enable/disable" toggle (`enable snmp access` / `disable snmp access`, and version-specific variants) per the [Plixer summary of Extreme's own guidance](https://www.plixer.com/blog/extreme-networks-enabling-and-disabling-snmpv1-snmpv2-and-snmpv3/) — i.e. an admin can disable v1/v2c entirely while leaving v3 active, which SignalScope's device-capability probing should account for (a `GET` failure under v1/v2c doesn't necessarily mean SNMP is unreachable, only that that version is turned off).

### Practical scope of SNMP write on EXOS

Not independently verified against a live switch this session; based on documented command surface only. What's clearly a **documented, intentional SNMP write path**:

| Realistically writable via SNMP SET | Notes |
|---|---|
| `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` | Standard object; expected to work per the same cross-vendor baseline documented in `standard-mibs.md`. Not separately confirmed against EXOS-specific documentation this session. |
| `EXTREME-SYSTEM-MIB::extremeSaveConfiguration` | An Extreme enterprise object explicitly described (via third-party MIB mirror, see `mib-reference.md`) as a save-configuration trigger — the SNMP equivalent of CLI `save configuration`, analogous to Cisco's `CISCO-CONFIG-COPY-MIB` pattern. Not confirmed against Extreme's own primary documentation this session (see uncertainty note in `mib-reference.md`). |
| `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticRowStatus` / static VLAN table, and Extreme's own `EXTREME-VLAN-MIB` tables | VLAN creation/port-membership objects exist in both the standard Q-BRIDGE-MIB and Extreme's enterprise VLAN MIB; EXOS's own SNMP MIB user guide is oriented around configuring **who can write what** (the `mib-view` mechanism, see below) which implies write access to at least some MIB subtrees is an expected, supported usage pattern rather than an incidental side effect. Exact confirmed-writable object list not independently verified this session beyond what's cited in `mib-reference.md`. |

Not evaluated this session (documentation not found or not conclusive): STPD/LACP membership via SNMP, port-security via SNMP. Per the architecture doc's general rule, **SignalScope should treat all EXOS actions as CLI-only except the specific objects above** until each is separately confirmed against a real device or primary Extreme documentation.

## Config-apply model

- EXOS is an **immediate-apply** CLI, same family behavior as Cisco/Arista/Huawei/Aruba and unlike Juniper's candidate-config model: every `configure`/`create`/`enable`/`disable` line takes effect on the running configuration as soon as it's entered — there is no staging area and no commit verb for ordinary config changes.
- The running configuration lives in RAM and is **lost on reboot** unless explicitly persisted, via `save configuration {primary | secondary | existing-config | new-config}` (bare `save configuration` saves to the currently-selected primary/secondary config slot). EXOS maintains **two named configuration files** (`primary.cfg` / `secondary.cfg` by default, `.cfg` extension auto-appended) rather than Cisco's single `startup-config` — a switch can be told which one to boot from, which is a meaningful difference for SignalScope's "what does Save actually do" GUI affordance: a naive "Save" button needs to account for *which* config slot the save targets, not just whether to save at all. See [Save the Configuration (EXOS User Guide)](https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/exos_31.4/GUID-96FE907C-FC5A-4E75-B632-002C6965139F.shtml) and [Managing the Configuration File](https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/exos_32.6.1/GUID-948439E8-14A8-4194-9A66-DD8D7D1C927A.shtml).
- This has the same GUI consequence documented for Cisco/Arista/Huawei in the architecture doc: an EXOS "Save" GUI action is **not** "commit my pending edits" (they're already live) — it's "persist the already-live running config to non-volatile storage, into a specific named slot, so it survives a reboot." SignalScope's GUI should surface the target slot explicitly per `gui-cli-snmp-mapping.md`.

- [SNMP MIBs User Guide section](https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/exos_30.1/GUID-F9C71D9A-4D53-47DB-B194-67ACB956BE37.shtml) — table-of-contents level only; specific supported-MIB list not retrievable via automated fetch this session (page appears to require JS rendering or a specific nav path not captured by the fetch tool) — treat as "confirm supported-MIB list against a live switch's `show version` / a MIB browser walk" rather than assumed from this link alone.
- [Setting SNMPv3 MIB Access Control](https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/exos_30.2/GUID-D57AEEBA-8942-4460-9704-01413FD52EB0.shtml) — confirms the group/view/access-model relationship described in `mib-reference.md`; full worked syntax examples cross-checked via search-result summaries rather than direct fetch (same JS-rendering caveat as above).

## MIB licensing / redistribution note

- Extreme publishes MIBs at `https://www.extremenetworks.com/support/policies/mibs/` and via the Extreme Networks customer support portal (`extremeportal.force.com`), which for several product lines **requires an authenticated account and, for some products, a serial/agreement number** to download. Unlike Cisco's `cisco/cisco-mibs` GitHub mirror (a clear, openly-fetchable public repo cross-checked for the Cisco assignment), Extreme's own MIB distribution does not present an equivalently unambiguous open-redistribution posture in what was findable this session.
- Third-party MIB-browser mirrors (`mibs.observium.org`, `mibbrowser.online`, `oidview.com`, LibreNMS' vendored copies under `librenms/librenms/mibs/extreme/` and `.../brocade/`) do host individual Extreme/Foundry `.mib`/`.my` files, apparently sourced from Extreme's own historical public releases, but **no explicit license statement was found this session establishing SignalScope's right to redistribute those copies** either.
- **Decision for this assignment: link-only, no files vendored.** See `mibs/` for the resulting placeholder and links. If SignalScope later needs live EXOS MIB text (e.g. for a MIB-browser feature or OID validation), the recommended path is to obtain the specific MIB from a customer's own EXOS software bundle (EXOS ships its own MIBs alongside the firmware image) or via an authenticated Extreme support-portal download at build/deploy time, rather than vendoring third-party mirror copies of uncertain provenance into this docs tree.
